item.title: Global solar installations face first annual decline in eight years
item.description: PV Magazine — China’s shift to market-based tariffs will drive most of this year’s drop in global solar installations, before cheaper batteries help revive growth from 2027, says GlobalData.

item.title: AI model detects small fires, smoke in PV plants
item.description: PV Magazine — Developed by researchers at China Huaneng Group, the deep-learning framework achieved 87.4% detection accuracy on a PV-specific dataset. It also reduced false alarms caused by sunlight reflections and demonstrated real-time performance on embedded hardware.

item.title: PV and batteries could help cut global power costs by 40% in 2030s
item.description: PV Magazine — A Schneider Electric Research Institute analysis of 40,500 scenarios finds that coordinated investment in distributed solar, battery energy storage and electrified demand could reduce total global electricity system costs by up to 40% in the 2030s, provided technology costs fall as projected.

item.title: Philippines approves solar cell factory from undisclosed investor

item.title: Denmark allocates $41.5 million to heat pump subsidies for 2027
item.description: PV Magazine — Denmark has allocated DKK 267.5 million ($41.5 million) to extend its residential heat pump subsidy scheme through 2027, alongside additional funding for gas network disconnections. The agreement also outlines plans to ban new oil and gas boiler installations and expand green heating support from 2028.

item.title: Solar, wind and batteries can deliver firm power at $0.086/kWh, says Ember
item.description: PV Magazine — An analysis by Ember finds that adding wind power to solar PV and battery storage systems reduces the median cost of meeting 90% of electricity demand from $105/MWh to $86/MWh. The cost could fall further to $52/MWh by 2050, based on the regional cost projections used in the model.
